subject: Ad-hoc DPIA evidence sampling & technical runbook request
messages:
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marin <legal@acmecorp.com>; Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 16:12:00 +0000
Subject: Ad-hoc DPIA evidence sampling & technical runbook request

Hi Elena / Acme procurement team —

Thanks for the heads-up on the DPIA review. To keep your audit sprint moving I can ship a small evidence bundle this week that answers the immediate questions the reviewers flagged. Can you confirm the items below are sufficient for now? If you need anything else we can iterate.

Requested sample (proposed deliverables):
- 1–2 weeks excerpt from the Article 30 processing ledger (CSV excerpt)
- Processing flow diagram + brief narrative for the payments pipeline (PDF)
- Subprocessor manifest for services that touch EU personal data (names + jurisdictions)
- Evidence of transfer mechanisms for cross-border subprocessors (signed SCCs or equivalent)
- Example KMS audit records (redacted) showing CMK usage for the relevant tenant
- Short technical runbook (how to reproduce the log export & processing ledger slice)

I attached an evidence-inventory-template (xlsx) so you can indicate priority and redaction constraints. If you want a focused sample (e.g., only Article 28/30 + SCCs) tell us which pieces are critical and we’ll aim to deliver in 48–72 hours.

Internal note: Marissa / Karthik / Grace, please confirm what we can extract without legal pre-clearance and whether the ledger extract requires additional data protection review.

Thanks,
Ava Chen
Senior Privacy & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference

Attachments: evidence-inventory-template.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Elena Marin <legal@acmecorp.com>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 19:08:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Ad-hoc DPIA evidence sampling & technical runbook request

Hi Ava —

Appreciate the quick proposal. For our external DPIA reviewers the priority is:
1) Article 30 ledger excerpt (we need field headings + at least 7 calendar days of entries)
2) Subprocessor manifest + any recent changes in the last 3 months
3) Transfer mechanism copies for non-EEA subprocessors

KMS audit records can be redacted for tenant IDs if you prefer — reviewers only need key rotation and CMK usage patterns. Also, can you indicate whether the ledger extract will include internal IPs or usernames that we should ask you to pseudonymize?

Target timeline: if we can get a first tranche by Wednesday (UTC) that keeps us on schedule.

Regards,
Elena Marin
General Counsel (Data Protection)
Acme Financial Services
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 08:34:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Ad-hoc DPIA evidence sampling & technical runbook request

Ava / team —

Quick tech confirmation: we can produce the Article 30 ledger slice without usernames (we'll pseudonymize user identifiers to a stable hash) and exclude internal infra IPs by default. The ledger lives in the compliance-db (schema: processing_ledger) and I can export a CSV with headings the reviewers need. That export will include: activity_id, purpose, categories_of_data, recipients, legal_basis, transfer_mechanism_ref, processing_location, controller_contact.

Subprocessor manifest: up-to-date list available (subprocessors_manifest.json) — I'll convert to a human-friendly PDF and flag any subprocessors with recent jurisdiction changes.

KMS logs: we can provide redacted audit rows showing key_id, event_type, timestamp, and whether the key was customer-managed. We'll remove tenant identifiers per legal guidance.

Timeline: if Elena approves pseudonymization, I can deliver the CSV excerpt + subprocessor PDF + runbook (short shell commands + SQL used to slice data) by 2027-05-18 18:00 UTC (today end-of-day for us). Otherwise we need 24 more hours for legal redaction review.

Attachments (internal): processing-ledger-excerpt.csv (sample schema export), runbook-export-20270517.pdf (example commands)

Karthik
Staff Engineer, Data Platform
Redwood Inference
From: Ava Chen <ava.chen@redwood.ai>
To: Elena Marin <legal@acmecorp.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@acmecorp.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Grace O'Connor <grace.oconnor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 10:21:00 +0000
Subject: Re: Ad-hoc DPIA evidence sampling & technical runbook request

Elena —

Thanks, that timeline works. We will:
- Deliver Article 30 CSV excerpt (pseudonymized identifiers)
- Provide current subprocessor manifest PDF + notes on recent changes
- Include redacted KMS audit rows showing key rotation and CMK usage patterns
- Attach a short runbook explaining how we produced the exports and how to reproduce locally (for your audit team)

I will upload the tranche to the secure evidence folder and share a link once complete. For convenience here are the artifacts we expect to publish: evidence-inventory-template.xlsx, processing-ledger-excerpt.csv, runbook-export-20270517.pdf.

Link (upload will be available by 18:00 UTC): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1aBcD_example_link

If you require a notarized copy of signed SCCs, Marissa will coordinate via procurement and DocuSign after the initial tranche.

Best,
Ava Chen
Senior Privacy & Compliance Program Manager
Redwood Inference
